prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Generate 5 ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question, each with a short title and a description of one or two sentences. Sample the ideas from the full distribution of possible responses, and give each idea its estimated probability of being generated (a number between 0 and 1).

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at timepoints during and long after a transient stimulus (e.g., wounding, inflammation, stress) to see whether AP-1-dependent open regions persist after the signal and AP-1 levels have returned to baseline.

ideas.title: Secondary challenge (priming) assays with AP-1 perturbation
ideas.description: Expose cells to a first stimulus, rest them, then re-stimulate and measure faster or stronger transcriptional responses; test whether inhibiting or degrading AP-1 (dominant-negative A-FOS, dTAG/degron) during priming only, versus during recall only, abolishes the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of memory-state heterogeneity
ideas.description: Use scRNA+ATAC (with lineage barcoding) to determine whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target-gene expression define stable, heritable cell states that persist through cell divisions and predict future responsiveness.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging of AP-1 dynamics and reporters
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or AP-1 reporters over days in single cells and lineages to measure pulse dynamics, persistence, and inheritance by daughter cells, correlating history with subsequent response.

ideas.title: Targeted epigenome editing and sufficiency tests at AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Use CRISPR deletion of AP-1 motifs or dCas9-based editing at memory enhancers, plus ectopic AP-1 induction, to test whether AP-1 binding is necessary and sufficient to establish lasting accessibility, histone marks (H3K27ac), and enhanced re-induction, including pioneer-factor and BAF-complex dependence.
